subject.title: fix(feishu): pace outbound sends per target

question: Should OpenClaw accept this Feishu-owned, default-off `sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` config contract without live Feishu API proof, or require live/redacted timing proof before merge?
rationale: The code shape is plausible and source-tested, but it adds an operator-facing config surface and message-delivery timing behavior where repository policy requires maintainer acceptance of the config contract and proof bar.

options.title: Require Live Feishu Proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until the contributor or a maintainer adds redacted live Feishu logs, terminal output, or a recording showing same-target pacing and distinct-target independence after conflict resolution.

options.title: Accept Seam Proof Explicitly
options.body: Maintainers may choose to merge after conflict resolution based on source review, fake-timer seam tests, and CI while owning the live-proof gap.

options.title: Reject This Config Direction
options.body: Close or replace the PR and keep the canonical issue open if maintainers prefer retry-only behavior or a broader limiter design instead of this Feishu-specific config key.

recommendation.title: Require Live Feishu Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until the contributor or a maintainer adds redacted live Feishu logs, terminal output, or a recording showing same-target pacing and distinct-target independence after conflict resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata names this handle as the plugin owner candidate for Feishu-owned behavior and config direction.
